--- /dev/null
+++ /home/agent/workspace/logic.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+LOGIC AND TRUSTED BASE FOR THE sort_list SPECIFICATION
+=======================================================
+
+1. Goal
+-------
+Formalize the informal specification in spec.txt:
+
+    For all input lists L, sort_list(L) is sorted in non-decreasing
+    order and is a permutation of L.
+
+Target theorem (see Section 3):
+
+    THEOREM main:  forall L. sorted(sort_list(L)) /\ permutation(sort_list(L), L)
+
+2. Logic
+--------
+Two-sorted first-order logic with equality (FOL=), extended with:
+
+Sorts:
+    Z       integers
+    List    finite lists of integers
+    Prop    propositions
+
+Connectives/quantifiers: /\, \/, ~, ->, <->, forall, exists, =.
+Inference: standard natural-deuction rules plus an induction schema.
+
+2.1 Integer arithmetic (linear integer arithmetic, LIA)
+Trusted axioms:
+    (A1) forall x. ~(x < x)                              irreflexivity
+    (A2) forall x y z. x < y /\ y < z -> x < z           transitivity
+    (A3) forall x y. x < y \/ x = y \/ y < x             trichotomy
+    (A4) forall x y. x < y <-> x + 1 <= y                discreteness
+    (A5) x + (y + z) = (x + y) + z, x + y = y + x, x + 0 = x
+    (A6) forall x y. x <= y <-> (x < y \/ x = y)
+A Presburger decision procedure may be used as a derived proof method;
+its soundness must be proved inside the checker, not assumed.
+
+2.2 Lists
+Lists are a free term algebra with constructors:
+    nil          : List
+    cons : Z x List -> List
+
+Axioms:
+    (L1) forall x xs. cons(x, xs) =/= nil                     distinctness
+    (L2) forall x y xs ys.
+           cons(x, xs) = cons(y, ys) -> x = y /\ xs = ys      injectivity
+    (L3) Induction schema: from P(nil) and
+           forall x xs. P(xs) -> P(cons(x, xs)) infer forall L. P(L).
+
+2.3 Defined function symbols (recursive definitions)
+Each recursion is justified by a termination obligation (Section 4, O1).
+
+    len(nil)             = 0
+    len(cons(x, xs))     = 1 + len(xs)
+
+    nth(cons(x, xs), 0)  = x
+    i > 0  ->  nth(cons(x, xs), i) = nth(xs, i - 1)
+    (nth is unspecified outside 0 <= i < len(L); the theorem never
+     depends on those values.)
+
+    count(nil, v)        = 0
+    count(cons(x, xs), v)= (if x = v then 1 else 0) + count(xs, v)
+
+    insert(v, nil)       = cons(v, nil)
+    insert(v, cons(y, ys)) =
+        if v <= y then cons(v, cons(y, ys)) else cons(y, insert(v, ys))
+
+    sort_list(nil)       = nil
+    sort_list(cons(x, xs)) = insert(x, sort_list(xs))
+
+These equations are the logical image of the Python code in sort.py;
+the translation claim is part of the trusted base (T4).
+
+2.4 Defined predicates
+
+    sorted(M)      =def  forall i j. 0 <= i <= j < len(M)
+                              -> nth(M, i) <= nth(M, j)
+
+    permutation(L, M) =def forall v : Z. count(L, v) = count(M, v)
+
+permutation is multiset (bag) equality. It is equivalent to the
+inductive "swap adjacent elements" characterization; that equivalence
+is a proved lemma, not an axiom.
+
+3. Main theorem and obligations
+-------------------------------
+    THEOREM main: forall L : List.
+        sorted(sort_list(L)) /\ permutation(sort_list(L), L)
+
+Proof obligations:
+    (O1) Termination: sort_list and insert terminate; measure is the
+         length of the list argument, decreasing under < (A1-A4 give
+         well-foundedness on Z bounded below by 0).
+    (O2) sorted(sort_list(L)):
+         induction on L with key lemma
+             sorted(M) -> sorted(insert(v, M)).
+    (O3) permutation(sort_list(L), L):
+         induction on L with key lemma
+             permutation(insert(v, M), cons(v, M)),
+         proved by case analysis v < y, v = y, v > y on the head.
+    (O4) Well-definedness of nth on indices 0 <= i < len(M)
+         (used implicitly by sorted).
+
+4. Trusted base
+---------------
+The following are trusted. Everything else - sort.py, the proof
+scripts, all lemmas - must be machine-checked against them.
+
+    T1  Proof checker kernel. A small program that accepts a derivation
+        tree and validates every inference step against the rules of
+        Section 2. It must reject unproved obligations (no "admits").
+        Trust: the checker's implementation is correct and auditable.
+
+    T2  Axioms of Sections 2.1-2.2 (FOL rules, LIA axioms A1-A6, list
+        axioms L1-L3). These are assumptions by design.
+
+    T3  Defining equations of Section 2.3. Accepted as definitional
+        axioms only after the termination obligations (O1) are checked,
+        which makes the recursions well-founded.
+
+    T4  Python-to-logic translation. The claim that sort.py behaves
+        exactly as the equations for sort_list/insert. This rests on
+        the operational semantics of the Python subset used (integer
+        comparison, list indexing/slicing/assignment, conditionals,
+        recursion) as implemented by the Python interpreter, plus the
+        stated correspondence between the code and the equations.
+
+    T5  The checker's own machine arithmetic (e.g., step counters,
+        hash values on derivation nodes) does not overflow; this is a
+        small, auditable implementation detail of T1.
+
+5. Minimality notes
+-------------------
+- permutation-as-counts is complete for finite lists; no stronger
+  extensional equality is assumed.
+- nth outside its valid range is left unconstrained; sorted quantifies
+  only over valid indices, so the main theorem is independent of that
+  choice.
+- No assumptions about Python evaluation order are needed beyond the
+  subset semantics in T4; sort.py is pure (no mutation of the input
+  list), so the specification is extensional and side-effect free.
